analysis.investment_thesis: Unified Data-Tech is a small IT services player with a dismal 0.36% ROE paired with a P/E of 21.1x — the math reveals a business earning almost nothing on shareholder capital while being priced for growth that isn't evidenced in the data. Without visibility into R&D intensity, client base quality, or a differentiated product moat, this fails nearly every point on my 15-point checklist.
key_strengths: High promoter skin-in-the-game at 60.39% aligns ownership with shareholders
Operates in the Indian IT services sector with structural tailwinds
Small Rs 619 Cr market cap leaves theoretical room to scale from a low base
key_risks: ROE of 0.36% is essentially zero — capital is not productively deployed
P/E of 21.1x on near-zero earnings implies meaningful overvaluation
IT-enabled services is commoditized; no visible innovation/R&D moat disclosed
red_flags: ROE 0.36% signals either massive equity dilution, earnings collapse, or structurally poor economics
Negligible institutional interest (FII 0.57%, DII 5.89%) suggests smart money is absent
No disclosed R&D spend or product pipeline to justify a growth premium
analysis.detailed_analysis:
My philosophy demands exceptional companies with durable innovation engines, 20%+ earnings growth, and ROE north of 20% and rising. Unified Data-Tech fails the fundamental test immediately: an ROE of 0.36% means the business generates less return on equity than a savings account, yet the market is pricing it at 21x earnings. This is the opposite of what I look for — mediocre economics with a growth-stock multiple. In IT-enabled services, without scale, proprietary IP, or blue-chip anchor clients, margins get crushed by TCS, Infosys, and thousands of mid-tier rivals.

Applying the Scuttlebutt Method mentally: I see no public evidence of a superior sales organization, no disclosed R&D-to-revenue ratio, no depth in management visible at this size, and no cost-accounting discipline reflected in returns. The 60.39% promoter holding is a positive alignment signal, but alignment without execution capability is not investable. I would need to see several years of 25%+ revenue growth, expanding margins, and a concrete product/IP story before this becomes interesting. Pass.
